around.headline: Bengaluru man strangled wife, spent 3 days with body before dumping it
around.summary: A man allegedly strangled his wife and kept her body at home for three days before dumping it, per The Times of India. Escalating control or violence at home rarely appears without warning signs — anyone who notices it, in their own life or a neighbour's, can call the Women's Helpline (181) or police (100) before it turns fatal.

around.headline: BWSSB's jurisdiction now covers the entire Bengaluru Urban district
around.summary: The Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board's jurisdiction has been expanded to cover all of Bengaluru Urban district, per The Hindu and The New Indian Express. Residents in areas newly brought under BWSSB should expect its billing and connection rules to eventually replace whatever local arrangement supplied their water before.
around.source: The Hindu, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Special trains added from Bengaluru to Mumbai, Karwar and Vizag
around.summary: Indian Railways has announced special trains connecting Bengaluru to Mumbai, Vizag and Karwar, including one timed for the long weekend, per The Indian Express and The Hindu. Worth checking if you're planning festive-season travel, since these routes fill up fast.

around.headline: Sensex, Nifty fall for a 7th straight week — longest such streak since the 2008 crisis
around.summary: Indian benchmark indices closed lower for a seventh consecutive week, the longest losing streak since the 2008 financial crisis, per Inshorts. If you invest via SIPs, the standard advice holds: stay the course rather than reacting to a single bad week, but avoid fresh lump-sum bets until the trend stabilises.

around.headline: 19 dead after drinking spurious liquor in Nagaland over two days; SIT formed
around.summary: Nineteen people have died after consuming spurious liquor in Nagaland over two days, prompting a Special Investigation Team, per India Today. A reminder to buy alcohol only from licensed shops — unbranded or suspiciously cheap liquor is exactly how these poisoning clusters start.

street_smart.title: You park your two-wheeler outside a busy market for what should be a quick 5-minute errand — just picking up one item. There's a small queue at the shop, so it stretches to 15 minutes. You only used the handlebar/ignition lock before walking off.
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds gave a personal, choice-based trap (today's real Bengaluru stories — a domestic-violence killing, a civic jurisdiction change, a market losing streak, festival trains — are tragedies, policy news or market data rather than a decision point a reader can rehearse). Rotating in 'two-wheeler theft prevention' from the evergreen list: this specific mechanism hasn't appeared as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The market lane is crowded and only partly visible from where your bike is parked; there's no dedicated guarded parking here, just a stretch of roadside where everyone leaves their vehicles.

choices.text: Leave it as is — it's locked, it's a busy public street in daylight, and you'll only be a few minutes.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Bike thieves specifically target factory ignition/handlebar locks because they can be picked or forced open in under a minute — busy daylight streets don't stop this, they just mean nobody notices in time. 'Only a few minutes' is exactly the window most two-wheeler thefts happen in, because owners assume a quick stop is safe.

choices.text: Loop a separate disc-brake lock or chain lock through the wheel/frame before walking off, and park where it's at least partly visible from the shop entrance.
choices.feedback: Correct. A second, independent physical lock defeats the 'pick the ignition and push/ride away' method that makes factory locks alone so easy to beat — a thief now needs tools and time for two separate locks, which most won't risk in a public spot. Visibility adds a second layer but isn't a substitute for the lock itself.

choices.text: Ask the shopkeeper or a nearby vendor to 'keep an eye' on it while you're inside.
choices.feedback: Risky. A verbal favour from a stranger creates no real accountability — they're busy with their own customers and won't be watching continuously, and if the bike does go missing there's no one to hold responsible. It's better than nothing, but it isn't a substitute for a second lock.

choices.text: Move the bike to the most crowded spot you can find, reasoning that thieves avoid dense crowds.
choices.feedback: Risky. Crowds can actually help a thief blend in and disappear quickly, and dense areas mean bystanders are focused on their own business, not your bike. Crowd density is not a real deterrent on its own — a second physical lock is.

takeaways: Always use a second, independent lock (disc-brake lock or chain) in addition to the built-in ignition lock — most thefts exploit stops under 10-15 minutes where owners rely on the factory lock alone.
Keep a photo of your RC (registration certificate) and a note of your chassis and engine numbers saved on your phone or in cloud storage — you'll need these to file an FIR fast if the bike is stolen.
If a bike does go missing, file a police FIR immediately: insurers require it to process a theft claim, and an early FIR improves the odds of recovery before the vehicle is stripped or resold.

quiz.question: Which civic body's jurisdiction was expanded today to cover the entire Bengaluru Urban district?
options: BWSSB (Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board)
quiz.why: BWSSB was originally set up to serve Bengaluru city proper; this expansion brings water and sewerage governance across the wider urban district under one board.

quiz.question: According to today's report, the Sensex and Nifty just posted their longest weekly losing streak since which crisis?
quiz.why: The 2008 crisis triggered a global credit freeze and a sharp, sustained selloff in Indian equities — the benchmark for comparing today's slump.

quiz.question: How many people have died after drinking spurious liquor in Nagaland over the past two days, per today's report?
quiz.why: Spurious or 'hooch' liquor is often adulterated with methanol, which causes blindness or death even in small quantities — far more dangerous than the ethanol found in licensed liquor.

quiz.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
quiz.why: Gujarat's coastline runs over 1,600 km, including the Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat, giving it India's largest number of ports among states.

quiz.question: What is the SI unit of electric current?
quiz.why: The ampere measures the rate of flow of electric charge; volt measures potential difference and ohm measures resistance, the other two quantities related by Ohm's law.
